prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your location in Atlanta, budget, timing, whether you need ductwork or a straight swap, brand preferences, and whether you value lowest price or long-term service/warranty. I can help you find highly-rated installers near you, but first here are practical tips and next steps.

What good installers should do
- Perform a Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old size”) to size the new system properly.  
- Inspect ducts and recommend repairs/modifications if needed.  
- Give a detailed written estimate comparing equipment options (brand, model, SEER rating), all labor costs, permit fees, and disposal of the old unit.  
- Explain refrigerant type (R‑410A for modern systems) and efficiency gains you can expect.  
- Offer clear warranties: manufacturer parts and labor, and a stated labor warranty length.  
- Pull permits and follow local code.  
- Be licensed and insured; technicians should be NATE-certified if possible.  
- Provide references or recent customer reviews.

How to evaluate companies quickly
- Get at least 3 written bids. Don’t hire the first lowball without comparing scope.  
- Check Google reviews, Yelp, and the Better Business Bureau for complaint patterns.  
- Ask for proof of license and insurance and for at least one local reference.  
- Prefer companies that do Manual J load calculations and show the worksheet.  
- Ask about financing, rebates, and energy-efficiency incentives (local utilities sometimes offer rebates).

Questions to ask every contractor
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation? May I see it?  
- What brand and model do you recommend and why? What is the SEER?  
- What is included in the price (new line set, pad, thermostat, permits, removal of old unit)?  
- What are the manufacturer and labor warranties? Is labor warranty in writing?  
- Do you handle permits and inspections?  
- Are your technicians NATE-certified? Are you licensed and insured?  
- When can you start, and how long will installation take?

Red flags
- No written estimate or vague scope.  
- Pressure to sign same-day without time to compare.  
- No permit pulled or refusal to pull permits.  
- Extremely low price compared with other bids (likely corner-cutting).

If you want, I can find highly rated local installers for you. Tell me:
- Your Atlanta ZIP code (or neighborhood)  
- Whether you need a full replacement or suspect repairs first  
- Any brand preference or budget range

With that I’ll pull together 3–4 well-reviewed local companies, recent ratings, contact info, and what to expect in price and timeline.
